morning.title: Aero India 2027 Sees Record Exhibitor Demand, MoD Expands Exhibition Capacity
morning.text:
In response to the significant rise in global and domestic exhibitor demand, the Department of Defence Production (DDP), Ministry of Defence, has initiated major infrastructure expansions for Aero India 2027. Scheduled to be held at Air Force Station Yelahanka, Bengaluru from February 8 to 12, 2027, the 16th edition of Asia’s largest air show and one of the world’s premier aerospace & defence exhibitions has witnessed exhibition space requests exceed initial capacity by approximately 12,000 sq. metres – a testament to India’s rapidly maturing aerospace and defence ecosystem.
Operating within the strict aviation safety and operational parameters of an active Indian Air Force training base limits horizontal expansion at the Yelahanka venue. To overcome these spatial constraints and accommodate the maximum possible number of exhibitors, DDP has rolled out two key solutions:
- Construction of Two Additional Hangars: Two brand-new exhibition hangars are being built to significantly expand overall floor capacity.
- First-ever Permission for Mezzanine Floors: To optimise vertical space without increasing the ground footprint, exhibitors will, for the first time in Aero India’s history, be permitted to construct mezzanine floors within their allotted stalls, wherever hangar height permits. All mezzanine structures will strictly adhere to prescribed structural stability, load-bearing, and safety standards.
The DDP aims to ensure that global aerospace leaders, domestic manufacturers, and innovators have ample opportunity to showcase their cutting-edge capabilities and technologies at Aero India 2027.

morning.title: Demand for Airborne Flying Testbed grows from Private Sector
morning.text:
India is seeing demand rise for the airborne flying testbed that was earlier limited to the public sector units, and now demand is also coming from the private sector due to limited availability. This is causing delays in testing of many of the airborne sensors and payloads that are being developed by the private sector companies in the country, said an official close to IDRW.
DRDO regularly takes on lease a modified Hawker 800 (BAe 125 / HS 125-800) business jets on wet-lease/service contracts as Flying Test Beds (FTBs) to test indigenous radars, sensors, and datalinks without tying up frontline fighter jets. HAL often uses Dornier Do-228 and Avro HS-748 as an airborne flying testbed, but they are not made available to private sector companies due to heavy demand from the DRDO programmes. Many companies are asking MoD to make available such platforms that can be leased by different private sector companies for their testing instead of them funding dedicated flying testbeds for their own programmes that could cost more to them.
Even if Air-launched weapons manufacturers are fully dependent on the air force for their weapons testing and leasing, air force jets are not allowed unless the air force also has keen interest in the product that the private sector companies are developing and the air force is backing the programme.
Su-30MK It is one of the most requested jets for airborne testing, but this is also used by other programmes, due to which it is hardly made available for usage by the private sector and needs to be cleared by both the air force and the defence ministry. Many of the testing of next-gen radars and pods are waiting trials or had to spend a lot of time after putting in a request for their time to be allocated to the flight testing schedule.
MoD might allow older Tejas LSPs to be used as flight testbeds for both private sector and public sector companies once they are free from being used as testbeds for the technologies that will go into both Tejas MkII and AMCA. ASTE has two Su-30MKIs that are often used for testing and validation of the air-launched weapons, and both Su-30MKIs will be used as flying testbeds to be used for the Super Sukhoi upgrade configuration, and chances are that availability of the Su-30MKI for private sector testing might be easily available in the near future as the IAF faces a growing shortage of jets that can be kept operational for combat operations.
India will require both business and cargo transporters that can be made available for testing of weapons to sensors for the private sector and also combat jets to validate many of the systems that they plan to develop independently, for which not only support but also subsidized rates need to be given so that even smaller start-ups that are working on cutting-edge next-generation technology have access to flying test beds, said sources close to IDRW.
RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: Indian Technicians Begin M88 Engine Training in France
morning.text:
French aerospace giant Safran has flown the first three Indian technicians who have been selected to operate and maintain its future new M88 engine MRO (Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul) base in Hyderabad to France for a four-month training programme that will build local expertise in Rafale fighter engine maintenance and overhaul.
The technicians will receive practical experience at Safran’s Châtellerault plant, where they will learn the disassembly and assembly of Module 4 of the M88 turbofan engine, under the supervision of experts from the base in this very demanding field.
“The three are the first trainees in a programme that aims to build the technical staff for the Hyderabad plant,” Sébastien Imbourg from Safran told AFP. After training, they will contribute to the creation of the Hyderabad facility’s first competencies and train technicians who are recruited and trained in India.
This is important because Safran is planning the Hyderabad workshop to be its first M88 maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) shop outside France. Safran revealed details about the project back in November 2025, with an investment of more than €40 million and an intended workshop area of approximately 5,000 m².
Safran, the plant is designed to ultimately perform overhaul work on over 600 M88 engine modules a year, supporting a workforce of as many as 150 employees when at maximum capacity. The plant will support the Rafale fighter engines operated by the Indian Air Force, as well as other M88 users.
This centre is likely to diminish India’s reliance on France for some of the engine maintenance work. Currently, for M88 engines that need work at the said maintenance level, India has had to depend on Safran’s units in France, but with this new workshop in Hyderabad, expert repairs will be available in India itself.
India presently flies 36 of the Indian version of the Rafale fighters with the Indian Air Force and ordered 26 of the Indian version of the Rafale Marine aircraft for the Indian Navy. The addition of the fleet will lead to an increase in demand for engine support, spare parts, repair, and maintenance staff.
This training scheme is also indicative of the long-term strategy of the Hyderabad project. Instead of depending solely on the technicians sent from France, Safran is starting to build an Indian team that can increase its responsibility in maintenance work, step-by-step. Its first batch will be crucial in both defining the work procedures and transferring the technical know-how to the following arrivals.

ADA Limits Aero India 2027 Tejas MkII Fighter Model Tender to 3 Firms
morning.text:
Only 3 organisations have been shortlisted by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA), so this is a Limited tender for the production of a 1:1 Air Force Mk2 display model for the Aero India 2027 show. It has been advertised for by the Ministry of Defence’s Department of Defence Research and Development.
These 3 organisations are; VEM Technologies, Tata Elxsi Pvt Ltd and Quest Global Pvt Ltd. No other organisations can therefore apply for this tender.
The tender to “Development of Airforce Mk2, Scaled model 1:1, for Aeroindia 2027 as per specifications” is available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). One unit is needed and needs to be delivered to Bengaluru. The time frame for delivery is within 60 days.
There are 2 tender references for this requirement. The first, GEM/2026/B/8300505, was advertised on November 20, 2026 and had an original deadline of November 30. A second reference, GEM/2026/B/8301926, was advertised on November 21 and has been extended to a deadline of December 1, 2026. It seems that this second reference is either an amended or re-issued version of the first. Unfortunately the exact reason for its issue is not detailed within the tender information.
This tender utilises a 2-envelope system, comprising both technical and financial sections. Offers will be assessed according to price. There is no reverse auction process available. Offers need to remain open for 60 days after the relevant tender deadline.
Whilst there is no need for an Earnest Money Deposit to be provided, the successful tenderer will be required to provide an electronic Performance Bank Guarantee of 5% of the contract value. This should be valid for 16 months.
As well as providing goods, tenderers must also provide installation, testing and commissioning services. All related expenses must be included within a tenderer’s price quotation. Micro and Small Enterprises and Make in India organisations are entitled to preferential purchasing treatment. Class-I indigenous organisations must achieve a minimum level of 50% indigenous content, and Class-II organisations must achieve a minimum 20%.
MSEs and start-ups are allowed complete exemption from previous experience and turnover criteria, provided suitable documentation can be produced. Make in India organisations can also benefit from preferential purchasing treatment within the defined L1+20 per cent range.
Whilst the tender is being administered by the ADA in Bengaluru, it is not a tender run directly by the Indian Air Force. Its aim is to produce a display model for the aforementioned 2027 Aero India show. It is not therefore for the actual purchase of planes, nor is it for the initiation of a fresh fighter plane development contract.
EDITED BY RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: IAF Wants Su-30MKI Fleet Upgraded Every Six Months After Super Sukhoi Programme
morning.text:
While the Indian Air Force (IAF) waits for final clearance so that the Super Sukhoi package for the first 84 Su-30MKI might start developmental testing and implementations, a senior Indian Air Force official speaking to IDRW has said that since the aircraft will serve the country till 2070 post the Super Sukhoi package, it will be easier for the aircraft to be regularly upgraded even though since its induction in 2002, Su-30MKI has been getting regular upgrades, but the interval has been far too long in between, due to which the aircraft is not the best flanker in the world now.
The officer told IDRW that the IAF expects once the Super Sukhoi package is implemented with the change of main radar and EW suite and other sensors, the platform should be able to get regular software upgrades every 6-8 months instead of years and LRU-level obsolescence management and EW/avionics box swaps every 3-5 years so that the platform can be adopted for newer weapons and sensors at faster rates.
The Super Sukhoi package centres on new mission computers, digital displays and encrypted data links that need recurring software baselining. Virupaksha radar will be first to be tested for the next 3-4 years before the system is cleared for production, but since the radar is totally locally made in the country, it will require regular upgrades, not every six months but every few years, to gauge its performance and look for further optimisation.
Super Sukhoi CCS clearance is still pending, with IOC for the first two testbed aircraft to be granted only about five years post CCS and FOC in about seven years after sanction, with serial inductions from 2033–34 being the right time when the IAF expects aircraft to start arriving, and by that time many countries might have started moving towards 6th gen platforms, and many of the 5th gen technologies that are being developed for the AMCA programme will also be made into the Su-30MKI, like its GaN-based AESA Fire Control Radar and EW suite that will be further optimised for stealth detections and operations in a network environment.
While software upgrades and improvements can be done in months’ time, they can’t be major hardware changes to the platform since it will cost IAF more money for their upgrade. Instead, the focus is on keeping the core platform hardware from getting obsolete.
The Airframe’s total technical life is now around 6,000 flight hours, with work under way to add roughly 1,500 hours, and HAL has extended the AL-31FP engine’s TTL from 2,000 to 2,500 hours and even has plans to increase it to 3,000 hours. IAF for sure has made long-term plans to keep the fleet active till 2070, which is four decades away from today, but since some of the aircraft are only 5 years old, alteast later batches will make it to 2070 as per IAF plans.
RAUNAK KUNDE

He said this facilitated a transfer of ownership without necessarily disrupting the broader market trend and could provide greater stability during periods of volatility.Mutual funds sold equities worth around Rs 34,929 crore in November, their first monthly net selling since August 2022. Data on National Pension System (NPS) investments for November will be available in December.Despite the November selling, Retail, MFs and insurance companies remained net buyers of Indian equities so far this year, with purchases of around 41615 crore, Rs 4.15 lakh crore and Rs 38,000 crore, respectively.SIPs Unaffected“Mutual funds' secondary-market selling should not be confused with investor redemptions. morning.title: The sky was once full of stars, kids; then the FCC let Elon Musk launch a million datacenter satellites
morning.text:
The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites.

The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.”

The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union.

SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less.

Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.”

The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request.

“SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters.

Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions.

Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “peak insanity.”

Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so.

Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create.

Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained.

Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites.

Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029.

Down on Earth, meanwhile, scientists trying to observe the universe continue to bemoan the obstructions caused by mega-constellations of broadband-beaming satellites. Proposals from across the USA, China, Europe and India currently call for around 100,000 satellites. SpaceX’s proposed million orbiters could run workloads which help us to understand the mysteries of the universe while also making them hard to see from down here. ®
morning.summary:
The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites.

morning.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
morning.text:
Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

morning.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
morning.text:
Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control.

Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year.

The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules.

morning.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
morning.text:
American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems.

The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23.

It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020.

However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted.

Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords.

The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers, targeted more than 100 water systems, with incidents reported across at least 12 states, and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers.

According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17.

Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. A CISA advisory from July describes this technique:

The authoring agencies observed Iranian-affiliated APT actors using several foreign-based IP addresses to access internet-facing PLCs manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and potentially other manufactured PLCs [T0883]. The actors used leased, third-party hosted infrastructure and manufacturers’ PLC programming software to connect to misconfigured victim PLCs. Inbound malicious traffic has been observed targeting PLC devices on the following ports: 44818, 2222, 102, and 502, as well as targeting modems on port 22.

These cellular modems, often installed by third-party contractors, frequently aren’t documented.

Unsurprisingly, the top recommendation for water utilities is to find every cellular modem in the environment, including those installed by contractors, make sure they aren’t exposed to the open internet, and put a gateway with multifactor authentication (MFA) in front of them to stop would-be intruders from gaining access via the modem and controller combo.

“Water utilities are spending time and money fixing the vulnerabilities they're told to worry about,” Securin CEO Srinivas Mukkamala said in a statement. “Meanwhile, attackers are getting in through equipment nobody knew was connected or passwords nobody bothered to change.” ®
morning.summary:
American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems.

Noel Tata says Tata Sons can't bypass rules for IPO
morning.text: Mumbai: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has said he’s against a proposed extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of Tata Sons, arguing that it can’t pursue a public offering without first converting itself into a public company and amending its Articles of Association. He has also challenged the validity of a September 17 board resolution on N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman, saying it did not secure the affirmative vote required under the company’s Articles.In a November 25 letter to company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay that ET has seen, Noel Tata also objected to the agenda for the November 30 board meeting, demanding that directors first consider his earlier notices on the Reserve Bank of India’s regulatory directions, the proposed restructuring of Tata Sons and disclosures relating to transactions involving group entities. This latest communication comes amid the ongoing turmoil over control of the Tata group with Noel Tata pitted against other directors of the holding company.136172071Also read: Tata Sons postpones board meeting to November 30On the proposed EGM, Noel said the board had unanimously resolved on March 21, 2024, that Tata Sons would repay its debt, stop accessing public funds and seek surrender of its RBI registration. “That resolution has not been rescinded, and the board has not decided to depart from it,” he wrote.He questioned the rationale for considering a public offer before the board had examined the September 28 proposal from Tata Trusts to reorganise the company, which he said was intended to address regulatory compliance. He also cautioned against making commitments to the RBI on listing without board approval, saying: “No undertaking, timetable or other commitment as to listing can be given to the Reserve Bank of India without a decision of the board.”Noel Tata further argued that any proposal to alter the Articles of Association or issue shares required an affirmative vote under Article 121. The board could not bypass this requirement by convening a general meeting, he said.On Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, Noel Tata said the September 17 resolution was invalid as it had not secured the affirmative vote required under Article 121 and Article 118. “A resolution of the board cannot take the place of either, and the company should not ask its members to act upon that resolution,” he wrote.He also questioned the proposed EGM to consider Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman, arguing that his reappointment as a director was already pending before shareholders. The annual general meeting was adjourned on August 18 due to lack of quorum, with the deadline extended to December 31. Until shareholders vote, it remains unclear whether Chandrasekaran will continue as a director, he said.Noel Tata also said a director whose reappointment or appointment terms were under consideration should not participate in the discussion or vote. “This applies to Mr Chandrasekaran on every item which concerns his reappointment or the terms of his appointment,” he wrote.Separately, Noel Tata said three matters he had formally raised under Article 121B had been placed sixth on the November 30 agenda, after discussions on RBI correspondence and the proposed EGM. He said the provision required these matters to be considered first and asked the company to revise the agenda.The matters include disclosures relating to dealings between TVS Motor Co. and Hanno One Warehousing, the constitution of a selection committee under Article 118 and the RBI’s September 11 letter, alongside the Tata Trusts restructuring proposal. The TVS-Hanno matter relates to allegations of conflict of interest that involve Tata Sons board member Venu Srinivasan and Chandrasekaran. The TVS chairman emeritus had backed Chandrasekaran’s reappointment at the September 17 meeting.Also read: Chandrasekaran to push Tata Sons IPO plan at board meet, company valued at up to Rs 18 lakh croreNoel Tata also sought a detailed management presentation on the Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s proposal regarding the monetisation of its stake in Tata Sons, including valuation, capital reduction structure, timeline and key terms, as well as the legal advice obtained by the company.He questioned how a quorum would be ensured at the proposed EGM, given that the AGM had been adjourned for lack of quorum. He sought the draft EGM notice, explanatory statement and legal advice, as well as confirmation on whether Tata Trusts, which together hold about two-thirds of Tata Sons’ equity, had been consulted.He asked for the November 30 board meeting to be recorded in full in audio and video, with the recording preserved and made available to directors on request. He also sought circulation of his letter and November 22 email to all directors and a response by November 26.The letter was copied to all directors of Tata Sons. Noel said his objections should not be construed as acceptance of the validity of the September 17 resolution or any item on the November 30 agenda and reserved all his rights and remedies.

morning.title: Semantic Prism: Generative Segmentation with an Explicit Semantic-Image Interface
morning.text:
arXiv:2608.11537v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Conditional image generators can render segmentation maps as semantic RGB images, but color drift and boundary mixing can undermine direct decoding. We present Semantic Prism, a framework that combines an explicit semantic-image interface with hierarchical refinement for road-scene segmentation. A generator adapted from a diffusion-distilled backbone produces a semantic RGB image with a single denoising update per crop. Distances to a fixed class-color codebook define interface logits and pixelwise class probabilities. Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment (HGEA) combines spatially aligned multilevel features from the VAE encoder of the generator with the input image, generated semantic image, and interface probabilities to predict additive corrections to these logits. Contextual Interface Hierarchy Disagreement (C-IHD) combines pointwise uncertainty, local context, and interface-refinement disagreement in a fixed score for ranking pixel errors, without an auxiliary predictor or an additional network pass. On the 500-image Cityscapes validation set, Semantic Prism achieves 72.07% mean mIoU, improving on direct-interface decoding by 11.39 percentage points. Extensive capacity-matched ablations show higher mean mIoU for multilevel refinement than for flat and single-level alternatives. The Cityscapes-trained model transfers to ACDC Dataset, achieving 46.89% mIoU without target-domain adaptation. Beyond Cityscapes, on BDD100K dataset, a separately trained model achieves 62.22% mIoU on its full 1,000-image validation set. Across the 3 evaluated datasets, C-IHD improves pixel-error area under the AUPR over uncertainty derived from maximum softmax probability, with segmentation predictions held fixed for each comparison. In particular, on ACDC, AUPR increases from 0.6580 to 0.7557, demonstrating that Semantic Prism presents more effective error ranking under adverse-condition domain shift.

morning.title: As Student Rollouts Continue, Visual Backdoors Keep Growing
morning.text:
arXiv:2611.22446v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Conventional knowledge distillation can facilitate the propagation of backdoors from teacher models to student models. However, how this risk manifests in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) remains insufficiently studied. OPD has recently emerged as an important post-training paradigm for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Unlike traditional offline distillation, OPD does not require teacher-generated responses. Instead, it uses the teacher's probability distributions to supervise response trajectories generated online by the student. Since the initial student model typically generates benign responses and receives no explicit supervision from malicious target responses, OPD appears to offer some inherent resistance to backdoor propagation.
  In this paper, we challenge this intuition and reveal a more subtle risk of visual backdoor propagation in OPD. Through experiments across multiple model families and datasets, together with theoretical analysis, we identify three main findings. First, unlike the relatively gradual propagation observed in traditional offline distillation, backdoors rarely emerge in OPD at low poisoning ratios. However, the attack success rate rapidly approaches 100% once a critical threshold is exceeded. Second, backdoor propagation does not depend on explicit malicious responses. Instead, it is driven by the continuous accumulation of anomalous probability mass assigned by the teacher. Finally, based on these findings, we propose a novel trigger design that enables visual backdoor propagation with zero explicit trigger injection. These findings further reveal an overlooked mechanism of backdoor propagation in OPD and highlight its potential security risks.
